submission.justification:
Radiator-R2 at 2 cm thickness provides the best pion/kaon separation performance at 10 GeV/c with a separation of 4.641 sigma. This represents a significant 16.8% performance margin over the second-best option (R3 at 3 cm with 3.975 sigma) and 58.3% improvement over R1's best performance (2.931 sigma at 4 cm).

The systematic analysis evaluated all three radiator candidates across the full allowed thickness range (1-6 cm). R2 demonstrated superior separation performance, with its optimum occurring at 2 cm thickness. At this configuration:
- Peak separation power: 4.641 sigma
- Well within the thickness constraint (1-6 cm range)
- All three candidates passed the humidity ageing test requirement (<10% transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent exposure)

The 2 cm thickness for R2 offers additional practical advantages:
- Reduced material budget compared to thicker options
- Lower cost due to less material usage
- Easier integration into the detector geometry
- Maintains excellent separation performance while minimizing systematic uncertainties

This recommendation optimally balances the primary goal of achieving the best possible particle identification capability while satisfying all technical constraints for long-term detector operation.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 at 2 cm thickness achieves 4.641 sigma separation, which is the highest among all evaluated configurations. This exceeds R3's best performance (3.975 sigma at 3 cm) by 16.8% and R1's best performance (2.931 sigma at 4 cm) by 58.3%.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is one of the three official candidates (R1, R2, R3) evaluated in the study.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: All three candidates, including R2, passed the ageing filter with candidates_remaining_after_ageing_filter = 3, confirming compliance with the <10% transparency loss requirement.
The recommended thickness of 2 cm is well within the allowed range of 1-6 cm.
